solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Love to get on lake shortly with pole to catch a fish

indicators.note: shortly asks for the word lake to be cut short before it is used
to catch means the surrounding letters close round the little word a

blocks.note: love is the zero score O, here taken twice over
the word lake shortened by its final letter
taken as written
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Someone tempted onto a lake with a fishing pole, hoping to land a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: OOLAKAN is a variant spelling of the eulachon or candlefish of the North Pacific coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The oolakan is a small oily smelt of the North Pacific, so it is a specific kind of fish.

clue.text: Lost lad at sea? Get navy veteran!

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy has gone missing at sea, so someone shouts for an experienced sailor to help.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an idiom for an experienced seaman who has spent many years afloat.

clue.text: Play at Headingley remained, Knight replacing Nasser initially

indicators.note: replacing tells us one letter is swapped out for another in the word for remained
initially points to the opening letter of the name beside it

blocks.note: lain, as in lain still, means remained
K stands for knight, as in honours such as KG
the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A cricket report: at Headingley the knighted captain came in for Nasser Hussain.
explanation.walkthrough: Headingley is the Leeds cricket ground, standing for Yorkshire, where LAIK is dialect for play. Nasser Hussain was an England captain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Yorkshire and northern dialect, to laik means to play or amuse oneself, often idly.

clue.text: Enraged about a right to seize and use property

definitions.text: right to seize and use property

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for enraged surrounds the a

blocks.note: a direct synonym
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone furious about a legal power to commandeer their possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Angary is the legal right of a warring state to requisition neutral property, paying compensation.

clue.text: Litter in Japan leads to Kyoto authority giving orders

indicators.note: leads are the front runners, so only the opening letter of each following word counts

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A Japanese city council is issuing rules about rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Litter looks like rubbish but means a carried couch or palanquin.
explanation.definitionFit: A kago is a Japanese palanquin, a seat carried on poles by bearers, which is a kind of litter.

clue.text: Matlo Herb afloat is salt of wisdom!

indicators.note: afloat suggests being tossed around on the waves, so the letters drift into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor named Herb at sea is held up as the wise old salt of the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: A matlo (or matelot) is British slang for a sailor, which fits salt in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Alembroth was the alchemists' name for a double chloride of mercury and ammonium, called the salt of wisdom.

clue.text: Enthusiasm from travel around America? Tons

indicators.note: around means the word for travel is wrapped round what follows

blocks.note: to go is to travel
abbreviation for the United States
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Someone's zest for touring the United States, and lots of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is a synonym meaning hearty zest or relish in doing something.

clue.text: Once rare, ground’s good for runs

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter stands in where another was

blocks.note: a ground for doing something is a reason
G is the abbreviation for good
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket pitch that was once hardly seen is now good for scoring runs.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of the word for ground gives way to G. Once marks the answer as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Geason is an obsolete adjective meaning scarce or hard to come by, which is what rare used to mean.

clue.text: Put an end to postie being mistreated

indicators.note: being mistreated means roughly handled, so the letters are knocked about into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged; a postie is British slang for a postman

explanation.surface: A call to stop the abuse of the local postman.
explanation.definitionFit: To sopite is an old legal verb meaning to settle or lay a matter to rest, so to end it.

clue.text: Orator let off becoming a bearer

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of kilter, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker excused from blame turns into someone who puts up with things.
explanation.definitionFit: One who bears or endures something without objecting is one who tolerates it.

clue.text: No Conservative managed article in the Sunday Times?

indicators.note: no Conservative means the party's letter is left out of the next word

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
to have coped is to have managed

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece complaining that the Tories had no grip on things.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the Sunday Times as an example, the paper carrying this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: An op-ed is an opinion column printed opposite the editorial page of a newspaper.

clue.text: Advance for Ayrshire milking facility

blocks.note: first meaning: money lent
second meaning: a Scots word for an open space where cows are milked

explanation.walkthrough: Ayrshire is both a Scottish county and a breed of dairy cow, so the second meaning is Scots dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum lent is an advance, and in Scots dialect a loan is a lane or milking green near a farm.

clue.text: Ballgame manoeuvre seen with hoops out of bounds behind back street?

indicators.note: out of bounds means losing the boundaries, so the outer letters are removed
behind means coming after, so the trimmed word follows the back street

blocks.note: an alley is a narrow back street
the word taken as written before its ends go

explanation.surface: A basketball move where the ball goes out of play behind a back street court.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoops is a natural basketball word, but here it just supplies OOP once H and S go.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley-oop is a basketball play where one player lobs the ball to a teammate who dunks it in mid-air.

clue.text: Ass almost changed direction in cobbled adit

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped
cobbled means roughly put together, so the letters are reassembled
in means placed inside the reworked word adit

blocks.note: to zig is to change direction sharply
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A donkey nearly turns round inside a rough mine tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: An adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The dziggetai is the Mongolian wild ass, also called the kulan or onager.

clue.text: Lawyer’s briefly right behind drawing

blocks.note: Att is the short form of attorney
R is the abbreviation for right
Scots for behind, also spelt ahint

explanation.surface: A lawyer's concise legal brief, right after a sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: Behind looks like a placing instruction but is the Scots word ahent.
explanation.definitionFit: Attrahent means attracting or pulling towards, as a magnet draws iron.

clue.text: Tough once managership changes, see me get dropped

indicators.note: get dropped means those two letters are left out of the longer word
changes means the remaining letters are altered into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the word taken as written
the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: A football club turns hard when the manager's job changes hands and I'm sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Tough is a noun here, a thug, and once marks the word as historical.
explanation.definitionFit: A phansigar was one of the Thugs of India, the strangler gangs whose name gave English the word thug.

clue.text: Rented right away and passed quickly over

indicators.note: away means sent off, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a direct synonym
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A tenant moved out promptly and hurried past.
explanation.definitionFit: To hie is an old verb meaning to hasten, so the past tense describes going over somewhere in a hurry.

clue.text: Ravel a little hard with tabor beating

indicators.note: to ravel is to tangle, so the letters are knotted into a new order

blocks.note: H, the pencil grading for hard, is a little of the word
the letters to be rearranged with H

explanation.surface: The composer Ravel writes a passage for a small drum, played a bit hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel reads as the French composer of Bolero, famous for its insistent side drum; a tabor is a small drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Athrob is an adjective for throbbing or pulsing, like a heart or drum that is beating.

clue.text: Book test in old accommodation

blocks.note: Hos is the abbreviation for Hosea, a book of the Bible
to try is to test

explanation.surface: Reserve an exam room in a historic lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: Book looks like a verb meaning reserve, but it is a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostry is an archaic word for an inn or hostelry, a place offering lodging to travellers.

clue.text: Row in shady ground for showy plants?

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of shady are broken up
in means the word for row goes inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a range is a row, as of houses or hills

explanation.surface: A line of planting in a shaded garden bed, chosen for bright flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ground looks like garden soil but is the anagram signal; the question mark hedges since not every bloom is showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrangeas are shrubs grown for their large, flamboyant heads of blue, pink or white flowers.

clue.text: Small employer saving money order for Durban pedlar

indicators.note: saving means keeping something safely inside, so the money order is held within

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
one who employs a thing uses it
MO is the abbreviation for money order

explanation.surface: A small business owner putting aside a postal payment for a South African street seller.
explanation.walkthrough: Durban marks the word as South African.
explanation.definitionFit: Smouser is South African slang for an itinerant trader or hawker who sells goods door to door.

clue.text: A trick absorbed by commoner with craft of an old Greek

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken in, so those letters sit inside the word for commoner

blocks.note: trite means common, so triter is more common
taken as written
a con is a trick

explanation.surface: A sly trick played by an ordinary person using some ancient Greek skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Commoner looks like a noun for a person, but it is the comparative adjective, more common.
explanation.definitionFit: A triaconter was an ancient Greek ship rowed by thirty oars, so a vessel of the old Greeks.

clue.text: A feast assists one worked up about nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, worked up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
about means going round, so the reversed letters surround nothing

blocks.note: a direct synonym
I is the Roman numeral for one
O is a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone helps an agitated guest calm down over a festive dinner about nothing much.
explanation.walkthrough: A feast is the definition including its article, an example of a Church festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Isodia is the Eastern Orthodox festival celebrating the Presentation of the Virgin Mary in the Temple.

clue.text: Quotes succeeded with lady about town

blocks.note: to quote a source is to cite it
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A society woman quoted in the gossip columns after her success in town.
explanation.definitionFit: A citess is an old word for a female citizen, a woman of the city.

clue.text: Talk over peer defending commoner

indicators.note: defending means guarding by surrounding, so the peer wraps round the commoner

blocks.note: an earl is a peer of the realm
an MP sits in the House of Commons, so is a commoner

explanation.surface: Discussions about a lord who has stood up for an ordinary citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: MP stands for Member of Parliament, who sits in the Commons rather than the Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: Emparl is a Spenserian verb meaning to parley or confer, so to discuss a matter.

clue.text: I sat out during gym being this?

definitions.text: I sat out during gym being this?

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of I sat are jumbled
during means within the time of, so the jumbled letters go inside

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
PT, physical training, is the school name for gym

explanation.surface: An ageing pupil sitting out the PE lesson wonders whether it is because they are too old.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: someone who sits out gym might well be too old for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Past it is an informal idiom for too old to do something well any more.

clue.text: Unchanged fare tails off for Chinese outfit

indicators.note: tails off means the ends are lopped from both words

blocks.note: a direct synonym
fare is what is eaten, food

explanation.surface: The same old menu is losing customers at a Chinese restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Outfit looks like a business, but it means a suit of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A samfoo is a woman's costume of jacket and trousers worn in China and Malaysia.

clue.text: Moderation in pub produces expression of contempt

indicators.note: in places the word for moderation inside the abbreviation for pub

blocks.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
an old word for a stop or moderation, as in no ho

explanation.surface: Drinking in moderation at the pub earns a sneer from the regulars.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoh is an interjection like pah or faugh, uttered to show disdain.

clue.text: Face a hare in hunting

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for the face or mouth
second meaning: the huntsman's name for the quarry hare

explanation.surface: Coming face to face with a hare during a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Puss is slang for the face, and in hunting jargon it is the traditional name for a hare.

clue.text: Military headgear very good? Not half, very good!

indicators.note: not half means only half the word survives

blocks.note: keen, as in keen prices, can mean very good
pi is short for pious, too good to be true

explanation.surface: A soldier's cap is admired, then praised with emphatic agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Not half is also a British exclamation meaning very much so, which makes the surface sound enthusiastic.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a French soldier's peaked cap with a flat circular top.

clue.text: Indian fellow’s old womanish and short of energy

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: anile describes a doddery old woman
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A man from India who is fussy like an old woman and lacks vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is a common Indian man's given name, so an Indian fellow is an example.

clue.text: Officers and workers following drill perhaps

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the workers go after the fabric

blocks.note: drill is a strong cotton fabric, and serge is another example of cloth
worker ants are a crossword staple

explanation.surface: Officers and men coming after an army drill session.
explanation.walkthrough: Drill looks like parade-ground practice, but it is a cloth, of which serge is another kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeants are non-commissioned officers ranking above corporals.

clue.text: Criticises clips reviewed in quick dialogue

indicators.note: reviewed suggests looking back over, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a critic pans a show
pins clip things together

explanation.surface: A critic slates film clips in a rapid-fire review.
explanation.definitionFit: Snip-snap is a lively exchange of sharp retorts, quick repartee.

clue.text: The sea bass has been dropped outside once

indicators.note: has been dropped means that letter is removed from the word before

blocks.note: the briny, or brine, is the sea
B is the musical abbreviation for bass

explanation.surface: A sea bass has been landed on deck and left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Sea bass looks like a fish, but the sea and bass are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rine is an obsolete form of rind, the outer skin or surface of something.

clue.text: Underwear and braces for guys

blocks.note: first meaning: a corset stiffened with bones
a further meaning: supports or props
second meaning: ropes steadying a mast

explanation.surface: Shopping for men's underclothes and trouser braces.
explanation.walkthrough: Guys looks like men, but it means ropes; braces is a third meaning between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are both a boned corset and the ropes that hold a ship's mast in place.

clue.text: Tormenter is gross and rather wicked

blocks.note: GR is the abbreviation for gross
ill means wicked, so iller is more so

explanation.surface: A bully is crude and quite nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A griller is one who grills, that is, interrogates someone relentlessly and harshly.
